title: Calibrating the natural-history model
text: package includes SEER-style lung cancer incidence, one row per age band stage: SEER*Stat gives incidence 5-year age band, case counts, populations, rates. model needs five columns (one row per age band stage): midage — midpoint age band, years (e.g. 62.5 60–64), Count — number incident cancers age band stage, Pop — population (denominator), years — person-time multiplier used form denominator (person-years = Pop * years), stage — stage diagnosis, two levels: "Early" early-stage rows "Advanced" late-stage rows. early vs advanced split modeling choice. Label early-stage rows "Early" late-stage rows "Advanced"; stages count early . paper used AJCC7 stage –II early III–IV advanced, might instead use SEER Summary Stage, AJCC6 AJCC9, different cut point (example stage early). handle unstaged missing-stage records likewise choice — paper distributed across early advanced proportion observed (known-stage) distribution. extra columns (age, Rate) ignored. calibrate different cancer site, export age--stage incidence SEER*Stat supply via the_data (see last section).
code: xlsx <- system.file("extdata", "lung_incidence.xlsx", package = "mbiedesign") inc  <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(xlsx) head(inc) #>           age Rate Count      Pop    stage years midage       PY         rate #> 1    00 years  0.0     0  5732775 Advanced     1    0.5  5732775 0.000000e+00 #> 2 01-04 years  0.0     0 23147084 Advanced     1    3.0 23147084 0.000000e+00 #> 3 05-09 years  0.0     0 28781431 Advanced     1    7.5 28781431 0.000000e+00 #> 4 10-14 years  0.0     0 29521104 Advanced     1   12.5 29521104 0.000000e+00 #> 5 15-19 years  0.0     7 31007881 Advanced     1   17.5 31007881 2.257491e-07 #> 6 20-24 years  0.1    30 30673778 Advanced     1   22.5 30673778 9.780341e-07

title: Calibrating the natural-history model
text: Two derived quantities one filter turn raw counts likelihood uses: risk multiplier one modeling choice worth dwelling . General- population SEER incidence understates risk screening-trial population, enriched risk factors (NLST, heavy smoking history). multiplier 3.1 inflates incidence reflect NLST-eligible high-risk cohort. parameter can change — different trial population, different cancer, warrant different value. exactly fit_natural_history() internally via cancer risk_multiplier arguments; block simply makes explicit.
code: risk_multiplier <- 3.1   # incidence inflation factor (see below)  inc$PY    <- inc$Pop * inc$years                      # person-years inc$rate  <- risk_multiplier * inc$Count / inc$PY * 1e5   # rate per 100,000 inc$Count <- inc$Count * risk_multiplier              # inflate the counts too inc <- inc[inc$midage > 0 & inc$midage < 80, ]        # restrict to ages 0-80  head(inc[c("midage", "stage", "Count", "PY", "rate")]) #>   midage    stage Count       PY       rate #> 1    0.5 Advanced   0.0  5732775 0.00000000 #> 2    3.0 Advanced   0.0 23147084 0.00000000 #> 3    7.5 Advanced   0.0 28781431 0.00000000 #> 4   12.5 Advanced   0.0 29521104 0.00000000 #> 5   17.5 Advanced  21.7 31007881 0.06998221 #> 6   22.5 Advanced  93.0 30673778 0.30319056

title: Calibrating the natural-history model
text: prepared data, calibration single call. specify two target sojourn times — overall mean sojourn time (OMST) late-stage mean sojourn time (LMST) — fitter finds transition rates consistent best reproduce observed incidence: optimizer arguments optional sensible defaults: k (default 16) — number states model, num_seeds (default 1) — random optimizer restarts; best fit kept, mean1 (default 3) — mean distribution used draw starting values, risk_multiplier (default 3.1) — inflation factor Section 2, the_data — supply incidence frame override provided cancer. Fitting runs maximum-likelihood optimization, takes little time; chunk evaluated vignette builds. package provides result exactly calibration.
code: # Equivalent one-liner (loads + prepares the provided data for you): fit <- fit_natural_history(OMST = 4.0, LMST = 1.35)  # ...or fit the data we prepared above explicitly: fit <- fit_natural_history(OMST = 4.0, LMST = 1.35, the_data = inc)

title: Calibrating the natural-history model
text: provided model lung, natural-history model calibrates cancer site. Prepare incidence data frame five columns Section 1 — midage, Count, Pop, years, stage ("Early" vs "Advanced") — typically SEER*Stat age--stage incidence export site, pass directly: OMST LMST targets modeling inputs choose — reasonable values depend cancer come prior estimates literature site; 4.0 / 1.35 used lung-specific. risk_multiplier applied data supply — scale appropriate target population fitting.

title: Reproducing the analyses in
text: vignette reproduces results manuscript, laid order figure table numbers. main analysis use NLST-like trial design — low-dose CT (LDCT) screening versus screening, three annual screens 4.5 years follow-last screen — estimate required per-arm sample size traditional intended-effect (IE) designs, together relative efficiency IE design. carry one-way joint-impact analyses vary natural history parameters, test performance, trial design. analysis shown base-case specificity (86%) repeated 100% specificity (reported supplementary tables figures). relative efficiency IE design RE=NTraditionalNIE, \text{RE} = \frac{N_{\text{Traditional}}}{N_{\text{IE}}}, values greater 1 indicating IE design requires fewer participants. Traditional rates per 1,000 randomized participants; IE event rates per 1,000 ever-positive participants; never-positive rates per 1,000 never-positive participants.

what: 2. Summary outcomes and sample size by design
title: Getting started with mbiedesign
text: get_summary_outcomes_by_design() main function. given screening schedule test, returns one row per design — traditional IE — late-stage event rates, required per-arm sample size, relative efficiency (N required traditional design divided N required design): relative efficiency 1 means design reaches power fewer participants traditional design. Pass design = "IE" return single design. row also carries control- screen-arm event rates (p_c, p_s), risk ratio difference (rr, rd), subgroup fraction design conditions (fraction — ever-positive fraction IE).
code: summary_data <- get_summary_outcomes_by_design(   rate_matrix = model$rate.matrix,   start_age = 62, numscreens = 3, screen_int = 1, num_followup_intervals = 4.5,   sens_e = 0.35, sens_l = 0.82, specificity = 0.855,   # test performance   allocation_ratio = 1,                                 # balanced arms   power = 0.90, alpha = 0.025                           # target power (= 1 - beta), one-sided level )  summary_data[c("design", "fraction", "n_per_arm", "relative_efficiency")] #>        design  fraction n_per_arm relative_efficiency #> 1 traditional        NA  17295.56            1.000000 #> 2          IE 0.3803904  10796.30            1.601989
